---
title: "Labs"
toc: false
---

Browser labs for the course's hardest ideas. Everything runs in your browser;
no installs, no server. Each lab follows one loop: **predict** before moving a
control, **manipulate** one quantity at a time, **observe** the exact
consequence, **explain** it in ordinary language, and **transfer** an object to
Stata for the problem set.

Every output says whether it is a live calculation, a stored simulation result,
or a conceptual illustration. Illustrative bands are never presented as
estimated uncertainty.

| Lab | Misconception it exposes | Lecture | Status |
|-----|--------------------------|---------|--------|
| Shock-to-Response Explorer | That a response is estimated from one episode | 1 | in development |
| Transformation Workbench | That an accumulated change is an accumulated level | 2 | in development |
| Identification and Controls Sandbox | That "I included controls" is an identification argument | 3 | in development |
| Instrument and Multiplier Laboratory | That a strong first stage establishes causality | 4 | in development |
| Confidence-Interval Coverage Simulator | That a narrower interval is a more reliable one | 5 | in development |
| Claims About a Curve | That "significant here, insignificant there" tests a difference | 6 | in development |
| Bias–Variance Laboratory | That a smoother curve is a better estimate | 7 | in development |
| Smoothing Workbench | That the fitted shape came from the data | 8 | in development |
| State-Dependence Laboratory | That an interaction identifies a fixed-state experiment | 9 | in development |
| Causal-Weight Explorer | That a moved coefficient means a moved response function | 10 | in development |
| Where Does Identification Come From? | That more rows mean more identifying information | 11 | in development |
| Clean-Control Builder | That already-treated units are valid controls | 12 | in development |
| Counterfactual and Sensitivity Workbench | That a reproduced calculation is a policy experiment | 13 | in development |
| Replication Referee Desk | That a matching figure means a sound analysis | 14 | in development |
